fact: UCSAF's chief executive said on 5 October 2026 that the fund will build 250 ICT laboratories of 20 computers each in public schools this financial year, that it has equipped over 1,121 schools to date, and that its subsidies to telecom operators have paid for 2,166 towers in 2,306 wards; the page does not name the law that set up the fund.

The Ministry of Communications and Information Technology tabled a 2026/27 budget of TZS 222,589,451,000 (about USD 89 million): TZS 13.1 billion recurrent and TZS 209.4 billion development, of which TZS 98.5 billion is from domestic sources and TZS 110.9 billion from external financing.

The article reports that the UCSAF tower project launched in April 2026 covers all 26 mainland regions with construction in about 1,400 villages across 688 wards, and that Airtel Tanzania signed a Phase 10 agreement with the fund to extend rural coverage.
UCSAF paid TZS 71bn of the TZS 126bn cost of the 758-tower rural connectivity project (the World Bank paid TZS 55bn), per the minister's report to the Parliamentary Infrastructure Committee.

The Prime Minister said the government allocated more than TZS 132bn in the 2026/27 financial year to the National Identification Authority (NIDA) for development projects, including 31 registration offices, a headquarters building and an ICT service centre.

Fungu 68, Ministry of Communication and Information Technology, was approved TZS 291,533,139,000 for 2025/26, of which development TZS 277,047,483,000 (TZS 98,480,905,000 domestic and TZS 178,566,578,000 external).

Fungu 68, Ministry of Communication and Information Technology, was proposed TZS 222,589,451,000 for 2026/27: recurrent TZS 13,146,172,000 and development TZS 209,443,279,000 (TZS 98,480,905,000 domestic, TZS 110,962,374,000 external).

The 2026/27 proposal of TZS 222,589,451,000 is lower than the 2025/26 approved TZS 291,533,139,000 (about 23.6% less); domestic development money is unchanged at TZS 98,480,905,000 and external falls from TZS 178,566,578,000 to TZS 110,962,374,000.

The minister's budget speech says 1,653 of the 9,124 towers built by private operators to March 2026 were built in partnership with government through the Universal Communications Service Access Fund (UCSAF).
